answer: Before filing, the filer must freeze the finished work in glacier ice and leave it on the comet ridge overnight, where the falcon keepers watch it. The desk measures the ice within a day: it must have melted one finger's width, proving the work sat there all night and was not made in an hour. Ice barely melted, a block with no keeper's mark, or work never frozen means rejection and a 250-coin bond forfeit, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 frozen nights plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims with ice frozen an hour before filing, and all forty were caught when the ice had barely melted.
